newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump, bonds rise as Fed holds rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump, bonds rise as Fed holds rates steady.

text.p: Stock prices jumped and bonds also rose Tuesday as investors cheered the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady.
But the dollar tumbled to a five-month low against the yen amid speculation that Japan would raise rates, making yields on Japanese investments more attractive.

The Dow Jones industrial average, which spent most of the session mired in the minus column, exploded in mid-afternoon trading to end with a gain of 74.58 points, or 1.03 percent, at 7,303.46. This was within striking distance of the record 7,333.55 set on Thursday.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,410 to 1,042 on moderately active volume of 447 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index jumped 22.64 points, or 1.69 percent, to 1,363.88 amid big gains in technology stocks.
News of the Fed's decision brought sighs of relief from stock and bond investors.
Analysts were sharply divided over whether the central bank would raise interest rates, with a slim majority polled by Reuters ahead of Tuesday's meeting expecting policy-makers to stand pat.

"It's good for the market short-term ... but it leaves some uncertainty about what the Fed is going to do long-term," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, adding it leaves a "cloud over the market."
"That's a guaranteed recipe for volatility", said Harris Bank/Bank of Montreal's chief economist Tim O'Neill, as the market gyrates with every piece of incoming economic data.
The Fed's next policy making-meeting is on July 1-2.

Bonds also rose, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury up 7/32, or $2.19 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.90 percent from 6.92 percent at Monday's close. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.

"There's clear-cut evidence the economy is slowing with no inflation around right now," said Martin Regalia, chief economist at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. "To have raised rates on the anticipation of inflation would have been extremely myopic."
Fed officials have cited wage pressures as a harbinger of inflation, but business and labour economists say the job market still has ample slack to supply workers at prevailing wages.
At its last meeting in March, the Fed raised short-term rates a quarter percentage point, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to ward off inflation.

In commodities pits, copper prices hit a one-year high amid supply worries, with the July contract adding 2 cents to 117.85 cents a pound at New York's Commodity Exchange. It was the highest price since last June.
June gold rose $1.20 to $343.40 an ounce at the Comex and June crude oil fell 40 cents to $21.19 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 stock index fell 37.7 points to 4,607.5. In Tokyo, the Nikkei average fell 156.92 points to close at 20,332.83.
